known_facts_book1: The mysterious ruler of the Emerald City, known as Oz the Great and Terrible, whom everyone believes to be a mighty wizard.
Receives each traveller alone in a different shape: a great Head to Dorothy, a lovely Lady to the Scarecrow, a terrible Beast to the Tin Woodman, and a Ball of Fire to the Cowardly Lion.
Demands that they first kill the Wicked Witch of the West before he will grant their wishes.
Is exposed as a little bald old man hiding behind a screen when Toto tips it over, and admits 'I am a humbug'.
Confesses he was born in Omaha and worked as a ventriloquist and then a circus balloonist before a runaway balloon carried him to Oz.
Ordered the people to wear locked-on green spectacles so the City would look emerald, though it is really no greener than any other city.
Satisfies the companions with tricks: bran-and-pin brains for the Scarecrow, a silk-and-sawdust heart for the Tin Woodman, and a drink he calls courage for the Lion.
Builds a hot-air balloon of silk to carry Dorothy across the desert, but the ropes snap and it rises without her.
Leaves the Scarecrow to rule the Emerald City and is never seen in Oz again, though he may have reached Omaha.

known_facts_book1: The Wicked Witch of the West, cruel ruler of the yellow Winkies in the western country of Oz.
Has but one eye, as powerful as a telescope, with which she sees everything across her land.
Sends wolves, crows, black bees, and her Winkie slaves against the travellers, and each attack is destroyed by the companions.
Owns the Golden Cap, which lets her command the Winged Monkeys three times, and uses her last summons to capture Dorothy and the Lion.
Cannot be approached openly by more than three summons of the Monkeys, and cannot harm Dorothy because of the mark of the good Witch's kiss on her forehead.
Is so afraid of the dark that she never enters Dorothy's room at night, and so dreads water that she never touches it or bathes.
Tricks Dorothy out of one Silver Shoe with an iron bar, which enrages the girl.
Melts away to nothing like brown sugar when Dorothy throws a bucket of water over her in anger, ending her life.

known_facts_book1: The Good Witch who rules over the Quadlings in the country of the South, both beautiful and young to look upon, with rich red hair.
Lives in a castle of her own, sits on a throne of rubies, and is the most powerful of all the witches.
Wishes to own the Golden Cap and its three commands over the Winged Monkeys; Dorothy gives it to her.
Uses her three commands to carry the Scarecrow to the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman to the Winkies, and the Lion to his forest.
Tells Dorothy that the Silver Shoes she wears can carry her anywhere in the world in three steps.
Kisses Dorothy goodbye and sends her home to Kansas with the Silver Shoes.
